forecast-period.text: A series of slow moving troughs will move over the west of SA on Tuesday then will across remaining parts of the state on Wednesday and Thursday as a couple of cold fronts move across waters to the south. A high pressure system will become established south of the Bight during Friday and persist there on Saturday. A trough will extend from WA over the far west of SA over the weekend.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Isolated showers and thunderstorms developing across the North West Pastoral and West Coast districts and the southern agricultural area, becoming scattered in the far west. Possible severe thunderstorms in the far southwest during the afternoon. Maximum temperatures above average in the south and west, grading to well above above average in the northeast. Mostly light winds in the south, tending northeast to northwesterly in the north.

Isolated showers and thunderstorms in the far west, extending to near western and southern coasts in the late evening. Possible severe thunderstorms near the western border. Fresh and gusty northeast to northwesterly winds ahead of a southwest to southerly change extending across the west and about southern coasts in the afternoon and evening.

Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms possible across most districts, but remaining dry in the far northeast, tending to rain at times over parts of the agricultural areas. Possible severe thunderstorms in the west and south. Maximum temperatures below average in the west and south but above average in the northeast. Fresh and gusty north to northwesterly winds in the northeast ahead of a southwest to southeasterly change extending across all but the far northeast corner.

text.p: Isolated showers and thunderstorms over the pastoral districts. Isolated showers about the southern agricultural area clearing late afternoon. Maximum temperatures below average. South to southeasterly winds, fresh near the coast during the afternoon.
Isolated showers and thunderstorms over the far west. Maximum temperatures below average. Southeasterly winds, fresh near the coast during the afternoon.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Saturday: dry in the far northeast. Generally 2 to 5 mm over the remainder of the North East Pastoral district. 5 to 15 mm is expected over the west and south but local falls of 15 to 25 mm are likely. Isolated higher totals of 25 to 40 mm are possible about parts of the far west, southern coastal districts and Eyre Peninsula, particularly with thunderstorms.
